statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band as December NQ futures hold a 43-point overnight range mid-band after the record Nasdaq-100 close faded off its session high.
recommendation: Tail at 10% maps to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The published forecast carries a WATCH band across the 17:00-20:00 UTC sequence on 7 October, covering the 10-year note auction, the September FOMC minutes and the following power hour, where Tail is modelled conditionally at 21-23%.
headline: NQ holds a 43-point overnight range mid-band after the record Nasdaq-100 close; Tail stays low into the September FOMC minutes
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 6 October at a record 31,224.69, up 148.24 points or 0.48%, alongside a record S&P 500 close at 7,818.93 and a record Nasdaq Composite close at 27,599.89. The cash session peaked at 31,361.37 and then faded roughly 137 points to finish near its 31,208.20 low. Overnight, December NQ futures trade 31,491.00, up 7.75 points or 0.02%, sitting mid-band inside a 43-point range of 31,478.00-31,521.00. An observed retracement into the close followed by a tight, two-way Globex band is the direct opposite of the no-retracement structure Tail measures, so Tail is assessed at 10%. Asian cash trade is mixed and orderly, with the Nikkei 225 down 0.29%, the Shanghai Composite up 0.31%, the KOSPI down 0.12% and the ASX 200 unchanged, while VIX settled at 15.01, down 3.29%, in a narrow 14.96-15.54 range. Stress is held at 45% because the environment beneath the record prints remains genuinely difficult. The Federal Reserve's H.15 release puts the 2-year at 4.84%, the 10-year at 5.31% and the 30-year at 5.66%, with current reporting placing the 10-year near 5.27% after a modest easing on 6 October and the long end still close to 24-year highs. Brent trades at 101.62 dollars, up 1.11%, and WTI at 90.34 dollars, up 1.01%, both recovering from five-week lows while UKMTO has reported at least one attack a day in the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Aden since 2 October; Middle East crude exports nevertheless reached 18.3 million barrels a day on Kpler's seven-day average, above the pre-conflict level, with about 40% of flows now bypassing the strait. Leadership is narrow and internally divergent: Nvidia and AMD printed fresh all-time highs and Marvell gained on a raised fiscal-2031 revenue target of 70-90 billion dollars, while SK Hynix fell 4% on earnings caution, SanDisk fell 2% and the memory ETF fell 2% against a 0.6% gain in QQQ. The dominant mode is recorded as mixed: the daily trend is up, yet the close faded to the lower end of the session range and the overnight band is two-way. The principal checkpoint inside the forecast window is the release of the September FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on 7 October, confirmed on the Federal Reserve's own October calendar and preceded by a 10-year note auction at 17:00 UTC and followed by a Governor Cook discussion at 19:00 UTC. Because the long end sits at multi-decade highs, a hawkish minutes read remains a credible repricing mechanism, so the forecast carries a conditional WATCH band from 17:00 to 20:00 UTC rather than a block. The shared Finviz context file was read and found stale, dated 29 September, with a partial collection status and both its calendar and futures sections unavailable, so it was excluded and this assessment rests on independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 8-16% through the Asian and European hours of 6 October, rose to a 22% peak at 15:00 UTC as the U.S. session extended, with the 15:00 and 16:00 UTC slots mapping to WATCH, then decayed to 10% by 00:00 UTC on 7 October as the index faded off its high into the close. Stress held in a narrow 45-48% band throughout and Confidence stayed at 86-88%, while the dominant mode shifted from mixed to trend-up during the U.S. session and back to mixed after the fade.
outlookSummary: Remaining Asian and European hours are modelled with Tail at 9-13% on contained two-way ranges. Tail lifts to 14-18% across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and the first cash hours for opening-range expansion, then to a conditional 21-23% WATCH band from the 17:00 UTC 10-year note auction through the 18:00 UTC September FOMC minutes and the following power hour. Risk decays to 11-19% after the 20:00 UTC cash close. Stress tracks Tail higher to a 53% peak around the minutes, and Confidence eases from 87% to 85% as the live price-path evidence ages. No post-event price structure is treated as observed.
